newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine business wants peso fall tempered.
newsitem.headline: Philippine business wants peso fall tempered.

text.p: The Philippine central bank should stop the further weakening of the peso against the dollar and also immediately bring down interest rates, businessman Raul Concepcion said on Monday.

Concepcion, president of the Federation of Philippine Industries, said unless the peso recovered and interest rates went down, "manufacturers will be forced to scale down their production output and prices will go up."

The Philippine peso has been hovering between 28.50 to 29 pesos to the dollar, three weeks after the central bank allowed the peso to float within a new, wider range. Prior to the de facto devaluation, the peso was at 26.40.
"Exporters were only expecting a peso-dollar rate of 28 pesos to $1 at the end of the year, but the rate today is much higher," Concepcion said in a statement.
He called on the central bank to compel exporters to surrender their dollars within 30 days from receipt, and only allow business firms which have to pay import bills to buy dollars in the market.

Central bank officials were not immediately available for comment, but analysts said monetary authorities were not likely to consider the recommendations, since the measures would mean a highly regulated market.
Domestic interest rates remain high as the central bank has kept a defensive stance amid speculative pressure on regional currencies.
The peso depreciation and high interest rates have forced oil companies to raise their prices by as much as 49 centavos per litre.
Concepcion said inventories at old prices will be exhausted by the end of the month.

"We want to prevent huge price increases, which in turn will trigger demands for higher wages, thus negating whatever competitive advantage exporters gained with the depreciation of the peso," he added.
